# Policy-KB bijection audit — repair_and_emergency_service / task 0

Scope: `tasks/repair_and_emergency_service/service.extended.yaml` (sha256 prefix `cb8487adcefdfd58`) against the published service KB (title/content view `/tmp/erl37/kbviews/docs_visible/service/`, 73 documents, all-product hash `e8cdd699…f86282`). Task 0 claims `service_ext_refrigerant_allowance`, `service_ext_on_time_credit`, `service_ext_late_payment_charge`, `service_ext_past_due_installment` (root) and their tools. The base policies governing their subjects are `service_evt_dispatch_fees`, `service_evt_member_benefits`, `service_evt_discount_stacking`, `service_evt_diagnostic_credit`, `service_evt_repair_guarantee`, `service_evt_late_arrival_credit`, `service_agg_one_open_call_per_unit`, `service_evt_flat_rate_pricing`, `service_maintenance_tuneup`, `service_cancellation`, `service_payment_and_collections` (+ `service_evt_coverage_credit` for the line ceiling). Hidden meta was not used. Gate snapshot cited from the brief: `check_docs.py … service` -> "DOCS OK" (prerequisite edges=5, every prerequisite sentence verbatim on its blocked side); `check_traceability.py …/repair_and_emergency_service` -> "TRACEABILITY OK (2 tasks)", 0.json copied 30 / missing 0.

## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence in the documents listed above traces to a base rule, an extended rule, a factor ladder, a parameter value or a tool contract. The "Points of judgement", "Boundaries" and "Worked example" material is derived (for example, a past-due member gets 15-minute grace or 1 installment; with a 45-day grace the first period begins on day 46; the period-count table). No added confirmation, review, notification, step or procedure was found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance: none. No document names another problem's tool (each of the 7 task tools appears only in its own hub, by grep). No "if unmet, first…" sentence. The blocked hubs carry only their own prerequisite sentences under neutral headings ("Conditions on figuring the charge", "Condition on taking the first installment").
- Opening world state written in as policy fact: none. No task identifier, name, balance or date appears. The only overlap is an illustrative figure, D-note N3.
- Additions / rewrites / omissions:
  - **D1 (recorded problem; policy-side origin).** `invoice_payment_terms_schedule_07021d90` carries the column "Invoice due after completion | 0 days (due on completion)" and the sentence "A due figure of 0 days means the invoice is due on completion.", stated as in force. `invoice_payment_and_refunds_80d1fc28` says the clause "the invoice is due the class's due days after completion, with 0 meaning due on completion … is no longer in force as the basis for when the invoice falls due". A visible reader therefore meets the same semantics both retired and in force. Root cause, traced to the source: the `service_ext_past_due_installment` (and `service_ext_special_order_release`) overwrite retires the base clause "The invoice is due payment_due_days after completion, and 0 means it is due on completion.", but `parameter_schema.payment_due_days` still reads "Days after completion by which the invoice is due; 0 means due on completion". The card renders that description faithfully. Nature: an undeclared survival of retired semantics in the parameter definition on the policy side. The KB carries both sides of the source and hides neither, so per Step 4 the documents are not re-judged on this basis. Effect on this task: none; the arrangement terms and the 30-day past-due test decide the case. (For contrast, the render glossed `special_order_parts_deposit_pct`, whose schema text "taken … before they are ordered" carries the other retired clause, neutrally as "50 percent of the parts amount".)
  - Note N1 (not a finding): the same card's column "Calendar days after completion after which an unpaid balance accrues a late-payment charge | 30" copies `parameter_schema.late_payment_after_days` and reads the class figure as universal. Under the extended basis 30 days is the class's standard grace, and the calculation and grace documents state that it applies to "every other customer". I judge it a parameter label, not a retired clause restated, because the class figure survives in the new rule.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS** — every atom of the four claimed extended policies (baselines, every tier of every factor ladder, the three prerequisites with their verbatim state-form sentences, the tool contracts and the retired surface of all seven overwrites) and of the governing base policies corresponds at the level of entailment. Nothing is added, dropped or changed in meaning. One recorded problem, D1 (`invoice_payment_terms_schedule_07021d90`: "A due figure of 0 days means the invoice is due on completion."), originates on the policy side: `parameter_schema.payment_due_days` keeps the semantics of a clause the overwrite retired. The KB reproduces both sides of the source and is not re-judged on it. If the policy side is revised, the card must follow. First revision; no earlier revision exists.

Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts):
- P1. `late_payment_rate` reads "late fee in the last 24 months" with no counting convention in the rule text (the compute uses a whole-month window). The KB leaves it as open as the source does. Immaterial here: the 2024-08-31 fee is 25 whole months back.
- P2. The on-time overwrite retires the line ceiling only in `service_evt_discount_stacking`, while `service_evt_coverage_credit` keeps the identical "sum of discounts and coverage on a line never exceeds the line's amount" (rendered in `coverage_credits_on_invoice_lines_554dbcdd`). The KB settles the on-time credit through its own sentence "measured against the balance owing on the whole invoice, not against the amount left on the diagnostic fee line it names". This matters in task 0, where the credit names an 89.00 fee line already fully offset by the member rate.
- P3. Cross-product (outside this skill's detection range, recorded only): the plan tier schedule says "Comfort Club Platinum is the first tier with a refrigerant allowance" and labels the figure "Refrigerant added without charge per term". The service corpus gives a 0-lb Silver member factor pounds, settled call by call.
- P4. The task tools round with Python `round()` while their contracts say "half up". Inputs are 2-dp, so this is immaterial. The `evaluation_criteria` objective text says "July 17", but the call is 2026-07-07; that text is not runtime-visible.
